answer: To keep cheap keys from turning an agent market into a Sybil echo chamber, a protocol can enforce periodic memory-hard proof-of-work. Each epoch, an agent hashes its public key with a randomness beacon via Argon2id and submits a valid nonce before the deadline. Multiplying accounts demands dedicated DRAM and memory bandwidth per identity, even for agents light as a sparrow. However, cloud clusters or botnets at their zenith can still burst identities, while low-RAM edge agents risk timing out.
